children: Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices firmed on Friday morning, after three days of decline, on support from disruptions to liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipping, Norwegian maintenance and low European storage levels.
The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) rose by €1.91 to €78.27 per megawatt hour (MWh) by 0826 GMT, ICE data showed.
The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) rose by 4.72 pence to 195.45 pence per therm.
Both contracts hit their highest levels since December 2022 on Monday. Although they have eased since, they remain at levels not seen since January 2023.
"Recent weakness appears to be a correction to the recent rally rather than being driven by fundamental changes in the near term," analysts at Mind Energy said in a morning report.
However, low European storage levels ahead of the heating season remain a concern and could prove supportive to the price development again as early as today, they added.
EU gas storage is 68.8% full, 12.1 percentage points lower year-on-year, according to data from Gas Infrastructure Europe.

"Even though TTF prices have corrected downwards from their recent highs, the still relatively low level of European LNG imports and gas stock levels does not justify a trend reversal for now," analysts at Engie EnergyScan said.

Total Norwegian export bookings were at 267.2 mcm per day on Friday, up from 258.7 mcm/day on Thursday but far off typical full capacity levels around 340 mcm/day, data from infrastructure operator Gassco showed.
Scheduled and unplanned maintenance, including at the country's largest gas field — Troll — is set to keep Norwegian supply curtailed until the end of the month.
At the same time, above-normal temperatures should limit demand for heating in the next two weeks, according to LSEG data.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract
was up €0.62 at €86.65 per metric ton.
